newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea warns of North Korean island action.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea warns of North Korean island action.

text.p: South Korea's Prime Minister on Friday warned of North Korean action against a group of isolated islands, and ordered security tightened at airports and diplomatic missions against possible terrorist attack.
"There is a possiblility of incursion into the five northwest islands," Lee Soo-sung said, referring to South Korean islands within sight of the North Korean mainland.

"We have decided to maintain the highest security vigilance on the islands," he told a meeting of security-related ministers to discuss Pyongyang's threats of retaliation against the deaths of its soldiers who landed from a submarine on September 18.
The military would be placed on maximum vigilance along the Demiltarized Zone, a buffer that has split the Korean peninsula since the 1950-53 Korean War ended in a ceasefire.
South Korea has long feared that North Korea may make a lunge for the islands, situated close to the 38th parallel that is roughly the line of division between North and South Korea.

The meeting decided to beef up protection of 395 key facilities, including airports, ports, communication centres and power plants against possible North Korean terrorist attacks, a statement from Lee's office said.
It also was determined to step up surveillance around 186 buildings of foreign diplomatic missions.
Protection of key South Korean figures would also be boosted. Spot security checks would be made around subways, department stores and bus terminals.
Immigration inspection would be tightened against possible infiltration by terrorists, the statement said.
"We will enhance diplomatic activities with our allies, including the United States and neighbouring countries," Lee was quoted as saying.

Tension has mounted since North Korea warned of "serious consequences" over the submarine incident in a border meeting on Wednesday with the U.S.-led United Nations Command, which monitors the Korean ceasefire.
It had previously threatened to retaliate "a hundred-fold or a thousand-fold" over the deaths of 22 soldiers who were among a group of 26 North Koreans put ashore on an east coast beach.
The northwest islands are seen as particularly vulnerable since they are closer to North Korea than the South.
A Defence Ministry spokesman said that although the military was on a higher level of vigilance, there was no change in South Korea's formal security alert status.

"We're just enhancing our overall vigilance for the nation," he said. "We've especially heightened security on the five northwestern islands. These are regarded as weak points for the nation's security."
"So far we haven't seen any signs of Northern provocation in those areas," he added.
In the first indication that tension was affecting South Korea's dynamic economy, stock investors on Friday began to pull back from buying.
"The North Korean threat has frozen investor sentiment. Investors have become conservative and defensive," said Cha Hee-gun of Sunkyong Securities.
He said there were no signs of panic yet, but Pyongyang's threat "made many refrain from buying shares actively."
